headline: Pretrained sequence models adapted with modification, region, and prior-knowledge structure
label: Task Aware Pretrained Sequence Models
summary: New preprints tailor pretrained DNA, RNA and single-cell models to specific readouts, from ncRNA generation to perturbation response and RNA-RNA interaction prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is adapting pretrained biological models to defined downstream tasks instead of relying on generic embeddings. Sequence-side work encodes biology into inputs or readouts: ModBERT uses a five-letter genome encoding of variants and CpG methylation, the mRNA study averages embeddings separately over 5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR, and MARRI adds opening penalties and hybridization gains to cross-RNA attention. Others tune pretraining scope or architecture: an apicomplexan-specific GPN trained on 455 assemblies helps P. falciparum epigenomic prediction, and B-RANKO is a 150M-parameter bidirectional decoder-only ncRNA model for generation and representation. A separate group targets perturbation response using frozen encoders, text and protein features, or knowledge-graph-guided flow matching. A comparison of fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome in admixed genomes finds parity with variant-based linear models.
